headline: Univer Builds Office Surfaces Into Apps
lede: Univer turns spreadsheets, documents, and presentations into embeddable product components. Its Canvas renderer, plugin architecture, and shared browser–Node API give teams a visual workspace they can shape rather than rent.

headline: AG-UI Gives Agents A Shared Interface
lede: AG-UI defines the event contracts between agent backends and user-facing applications. Streaming messages, synchronized state, generative interfaces, and human approvals become modular parts in a transport-agnostic system.

headline: Stitch Skills Draw A Line To Production
lede: Stitch Skills maps the route from generated screens to working frontend code. Its agent plugins handle design systems, themes, assets, specifications, and React-based builds as a repeatable construction workflow.

headline: Plannotator Brings Agents Under Review
lede: Plannotator places a local review layer between coding agents and their output. Plans, patches, documents, and decisions stay organized for human inspection, with structured feedback sent back without surrendering the workflow to a remote service.

headline: Chrome DevTools Puts Agents In The Browser
lede: Chrome DevTools MCP gives coding agents a live browser, not just a text window. Through its CLI and MCP server, agents can navigate, inspect networks, read console output, capture evidence, and measure real performance.

headline: Open Code Review Traces Defects To Lines
lede: Open Code Review combines deterministic file selection with an LLM investigator that can search across a codebase. The result is a review pipeline built for precise locations, cross-file context, resumable sessions, and configurable security rules.

headline: LoopForge Turns Agent Work Into Operations
lede: LoopForge organizes coding agents as explicit delivery machinery. Docker workspaces, role-based tasks, approval nodes, checkpoints, artifacts, and retries give teams a controlled path from a request to a branch or pull request.

headline: ggml Makes Efficient Inference Portable
lede: ggml strips tensor computation down to portable C and C++ with no external dependencies. Quantization, architecture-specific kernels, and multiple CPU, GPU, NPU, and browser backends make constrained inference a systems problem it can actually solve.

headline: Claude-BugHunter Packages The Huntbook
lede: Claude-BugHunter assembles authorized security testing into a structured agent skill set. Reconnaissance, vulnerability validation, evidence capture, and reporting are organized into reusable procedures, with explicit boundaries around scope and misuse.

headline: Modern Web Guidance Updates The Agent Shelf
lede: Modern Web Guidance curates browser knowledge for both developers and coding agents. Searchable guides cover platform APIs, accessibility, performance, and compatibility while helping teams replace inherited patterns with native web capabilities.
